reason: The passage establishes and emphasizes multiple hierarchical structures: (1) Paternal authority - Isaac possesses power to confer blessings that grant dominance; (2) Age-based hierarchy - Esau is explicitly identified as 'הַגָּדֹל' (the elder/greater), with Jacob as the younger; (3) Primogeniture - references to 'בְּכוֹרָה' (birthright) establish the firstborn's privileged status; (4) Parental command structure - both Isaac and Rebekah issue commands to their sons expecting obedience; (5) The blessing itself explicitly emphasizes dominance, stating the recipient will have peoples serve him ('יַֽעַבְד֣וּךָ עַמִּ֗ים') and be 'גְבִיר' (master) over his brothers. While the narrative involves transgression of the expected hierarchy through deception, the passage structure, terminology, and blessing all fundamentally emphasize hierarchical authority relationships.
